production.note: US model years 1995-1996: owner decision, 10 October 2026. Evidence: RM Sotheby's sells a '1995 Ferrari F50', 'one of just 55 US-delivery examples', 'Completed on 21 December 1995' (rm-f50); Car and Driver tested a '1996 Ferrari F50' (read by the project owner on 9 October 2026, caranddriver-f50-1996-test). Build years were 1995-1997: Evo, 'Just 349 were built between 1995 and 1997' (evo-f50).

body.note: Two-seat mid-engined open car; Evo: it 'wasn't a fixed-head coupe', with a removable Targa panel. No fixed-roof version, and Ferrari did not sell it as a Targa, so Roadster. Car and Driver's test (owner-read) calls it a roadster.

displacementL.note: 4,698 cc. Evo panel: '4698cc, V12'; Car and Driver test panel (owner-read): 'Displacement: 287 in3, 4698 cm3'.

aspiration.note: Evo: 'the most glorious naturally aspirated V12'.

fuel.note: Petrol V12; inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: Mid-mounted V12 driving the rear wheels; inferred from the description.

transmission.note: Evo: 'six-speed manual 'box'; Car and Driver test panel (owner-read): '6-speed manual'.

powerHp.note: Owner decision, 9 October 2026: Car and Driver's values are used. Car and Driver test panel for a 1996 F50, read by the project owner on 9 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools): "Power: 513 hp @ 8500 rpm". This equals Ferrari's metric rating converted (520 PS x 0.98632 = 513 hp): auto.cz (Karel Haas, 2006): "Maximální výkon motoru | 383 kW (520 k) / 8500 min-1" (autocz-f50). Evo's specification panel: "Power: 513bhp @ 8500rpm" (evo-f50). RM Sotheby's, US-delivery car: 'the high-compression V-12 in the F50 developed 513 horsepower' (rm-f50). No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: Weight-order step 2: Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision, 9 October 2026, docs/DATA_GUIDE.md). Owner decision, 9 October 2026: Car and Driver's tested figure used. Car and Driver test panel for a 1996 F50, read by the project owner on 9 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools): "Curb Weight: 3080 lb" (a measured weight of the test car, labelled tested). No other figure agrees within 2%: the widely printed 1,230 kg (2,712 lb) is labelled dry by some sources and kerb by others, and Sports Car Bible's 1,320 kg (2,910 lb) is unlabelled; see discrepancies.

values.value: 1,230 kg labelled dry: 'Dry Weight : 2712 lbs / 1230 kg'

discrepancies.reason: Basis unknown. 1,230 kg is about 12% below Car and Driver's scale weight and is called dry by one source and kerb by another, so it is probably a dry weight; Sports Car Bible's 1,320 kg is unlabelled and unattributed. A forum post (not citable) says the owner's manual lists 2,712 lb. Sports Car Bible (an enthusiast site, not cited in a full record) prints an unlabelled 2,910 lb / 1,320 kg.
discrepancies.resolution: Owner decision, 9 October 2026: Car and Driver's tested figure used. A Ferrari figure, if found, would take priority (step 1).

reviewNotes: US model years are unconfirmed: production 1995-1997 are build years (Evo); a US-delivery car is titled 1995 (RM Sotheby's) and Car and Driver tested a 1996 car.
